explanations: There is no defect. Each attempt gets its own AbortController and timer, cleared in finally. Only network errors, timeouts, 429/502/503/504 and OVER_QUERY_LIMIT are retried, with bounded exponential backoff and jitter; the request is a read, so retrying is safe. Other HTTP errors become RoutingUnavailableError immediately, ZERO_RESULTS becomes RouteNotFoundError, and provider-specific types never leak past the adapter. The service degrades to a haversine estimate only for availability failures, not for unroutable trips.

400 is not in RETRYABLE_HTTP, so callOnce hits the !res.ok branch and throws RoutingUnavailableError. estimate() rethrows any non-RetryableError at once, so there is no retry. RouteNotFoundError is only for ZERO_RESULTS or empty routes, and no estimate is produced.

Timeouts abort fetch, which callOnce wraps as RetryableError. After maxAttempts the adapter throws RoutingUnavailableError, which the service catches and turns into a haversine-based estimate with source 'fallback'. There is no cache, and the fallback happens only after all attempts.

toEstimate sums per leg, using duration_in_traffic when present and duration otherwise, and sets trafficAware to false as soon as any leg lacks traffic data. It never discards a leg or ignores available traffic data.
